Injective iff trivial kernel is true for ring homomorphisms. Q is not an ideal of R: 1 is in Q, but sqrt(2)*1 is not.

Assuming commutative rings with unity, both statements are true (A). Without unity or commutativity, Statement 1 fails, e.g. 4Z is maximal but not prime in 2Z, which gives D. If unity is not assumed, Statement 2 also fails (2Z/4Z is not a field), which gives B.

Statement 2 is true: an injective operator on a finite-dimensional space is bijective. Read literally, 'dim V < dim W < 1' can never hold, so Statement 1 is vacuously true (A). The likely intent was '< infinity', where the zero map is a counterexample, making Statement 1 false (D).
A quotient of a commutative ring is commutative. An ideal contains 1 iff it is all of R: 1 in N gives r = r*1 in N for every r.
Europa's cracks and lineae come from tidal flexing and tectonic-style movement of the ice shell, not from volcanism, impacts or solar flares.

No single standard 'six dimensions' list exists: PESTLE, and Pride & Ferrell's list with competitive and regulatory forces, both qualify. Several options fall outside any of them: B (weather), C (the marketing team's preferences), G (global factors) and, depending on the text, H or I. C is the only one that is clearly internal. G is plausible if the intended list is PESTLE.

Work specialisation, also called division of labour, splits a task so no one person does all of it (textbook definition). H (work division), B (workload balancing) and C (work distribution) are close synonyms and also defensible.

The economic perspective grew out of limits-to-growth carrying-capacity models: overuse of resources, overpopulation and over-pollution. It contrasts with the environmental perspective. F uses the wrong perspective label.

The rate is (4000-400)/72000 = $0.05 per mile, so yearly depreciation is 1000, 1250, 900 and 450. It differs each year, so 'the depreciation per year' has no single value. B matches only year 1, and H ($3,600) is the four-year total.
